<reason>Both sides were disciplined, engaged the motion as written, and progressed rather than repeated. PRO's best move was the reframe of enforcement from foreign inspection to home-state parentage/passport leverage plus home-domiciled instruments (escrow, panel counsel, licensed insurer, revocable listing), and its closing risk-asymmetry weighing was the strongest single piece of weighing on the table. But CON's pressure question forced the pivotal concession: PRO conceded "the child comes home," which dissolved the absolute version of its own claim in [A2.3]/[A2.4] that unaccredited clinics "cannot sell the only thing the client actually needs." Once deliverability is no longer binding, CON's "respectable storefront in front of the grey market" mechanism survives largely intact, and CON tied that directly to the motion's own load-bearing condition — a standard that cannot be enforced without either stranding newborns or firing blanks is permission dressed as safeguard. CON also handled PRO's counter-pressure honestly and consistently (blinking is a response to child-harm, not to adult penalties; no mechanism for the already-pregnant woman, only volume reduction), and used the organ-trade frame coherently across all rounds rather than as a one-off analogy. PRO's fallback to "friction, not statelessness" and "a leaky mechanism still catches something" retains real force — escrow and insurer coverage genuinely protect the compliant subset — and CON slightly overclaims in closing that "what is enforceable is nothing," ignoring PRO's non-parentage instruments. CON's rebuttal 2 was also clipped, a minor execution cost. Net: CON exposed and exploited the more damaging concession, and made the decision rule cleaner, for a clear but competitive win.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Q1 dilemma (refuse the child or reveal the threat as empty) and its follow-up in [B4.2]-[B4.5]: PRO's honest "the child comes home" answer was turned into a direct kill on PRO's earlier claim that cost is not the binding constraint, reviving the unaccredited-clinic-undercutting argument by PRO's own hand.</best_rebuttal>
